headline: Tangail youth killed while fighting for Russia in Ukraine war
summary: Mridul Khan, 22, was reportedly killed in a drone attack near the Ukrainian border, his family claims he was deceived into military service.
details: A 22-year-old man from Kalihati upazila in Tangail, Mridul Khan, has reportedly been killed while fighting in the Russia-Ukraine war, according to his family.
Family members state that Mridul was killed in a drone attack near the Ukrainian border on Saturday night, though the claim has not yet been officially confirmed by diplomatic sources.
Mridul's father, Sayeed Khan, alleged that his son travelled to Russia on January 29 via a recruiting agency after being promised a job at a cattle farm.
The father claims that upon arrival, Mridul was instead forced into the Russian military through a broker network and sent to the front lines after completing training.
Sayeed Khan added that his son had previously posted a war-related video on social media and was subsequently threatened by brokers.
The grieving family is now demanding that the government bring Mridul's body home and take legal action against the brokers responsible for the deception.
Local authorities, including the Kalihati Upazila Nirbahi Officer and the Police Station Officer-in-Charge, stated they have heard of the incident but have received no official information.

headline_marked: Supreme Court [[scraps ruling allowing dental technologists to see patients]] independently
headline: Supreme Court scraps ruling allowing dental technologists to see patients independently
summary: The Appellate Division has overturned a High Court decision, meaning diploma-holders cannot now open private chambers or prescribe treatment.
details: The Supreme Court's top appeals bench has overturned a High Court ruling that allowed diploma-holding dental assistants and dental technologists to practise privately.
A full bench of the Appellate Division, led by the chief justice, passed the order on Wednesday after allowing an appeal filed by the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (BMDC).
Under the new ruling, dental technologists will now be allowed to work only as assistants under registered dental surgeons.
This means they will no longer be able to open their own private chambers, see patients independently or prescribe medical treatment.
caption:
Can dental technologists practice independently? The Supreme Court says no.

The Supreme Court's top appeals bench has overturned a High Court ruling that allowed diploma-holding dental assistants and dental technologists to practise privately.

A full bench of the Appellate Division, led by the chief justice, passed the order on Wednesday after allowing an appeal filed by the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (BMDC).

Under the new ruling, dental technologists will now be allowed to work only as assistants under registered dental surgeons.

This means they will no longer be able to open their own private chambers, see patients independently or prescribe medical treatment.
